title: A Trail for the Current
premise: Riverboat captain Sable Nystrom salvages a sealed chest from a wrecked barge, stamped with the seal of Vhaloria—a nation erased from maps forty years ago. Inside are documents pointing to a hidden archive at the river's forbidden source, and a dying stranger's plea that she deliver them. Hunted by a government ministry that wants the past buried and shadowed by an exiled Vhalorian archivist named Ivo Kestrel, Sable navigates rapids, betrayals, and her own grief for a lost crew as the monsoon season closes in. At the source, she must choose between surrendering the chest to save her found family or opening the archive that could resurrect a dead nation—and discovers the current always returns what it takes.
about_author: Sebastian Underhill is the pen name of a former inland waterways surveyor who spent a decade charting rivers that appear on no tourist map. He writes adventure fiction from a houseboat he refuses to name publicly.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Receipts
chapters.summary: Sable Nystrom pilots her aging riverboat, the Magpie, through low-water shoals with her ragtag crew: engineer Doss, cook Marisol, and deckhand Pip. Salvaging a snagged barge after a storm, they haul up a lead-lined chest stamped with a seal none of them recognize—except Pip, who goes pale and lies about it. POV: Sable. Beat: uneasy curiosity; the ordinary world cracks open.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Wax
chapters.summary: Below decks, Sable pries the chest open against Doss's warnings. Inside: ledgers, a brass astrolabe of impossible craftsmanship, and a letter addressed to 'the keeper at the source.' Pip confesses his grandmother was Vhalorian, purged in the Erasure, and that carrying the seal is a hanging offense. POV: Sable. Beat: dread mixed with wonder; duty to the law versus duty to the dead.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Upstream
chapters.summary: At the Corben Landing market, a wounded stranger collapses onto the Magpie's gangplank clutching half a Vhalorian route-map. Before dying, he tells Sable the archive at the source holds the names of everyone the Erasure deleted—and begs her to finish his delivery. Ministry agents arrive asking questions. POV: Sable. Beat: grief and complicity; she can no longer pretend ignorance.

chapters.title: Ministry Men and Mud
chapters.summary: Inspector Calloway Brant boards the Magpie under pretext of a salvage audit, courteous and cold. He knows about the chest—or suspects. Sable stonewalls while Marisol hides the documents in a flour barrel. After Brant leaves, they find a tracking beacon wired to their hull. POV: Sable. Beat: paranoia takes root; the hunt has begun.

chapters.title: Ivo Kestrel Buys a Drink
chapters.summary: In a dockside tavern, an archivist with a forged passport introduces himself: Ivo Kestrel, last trained keeper of the Vhalorian archive, exiled since childhood. He offers Sable a fortune in recovered bullion to run him upstream past three closed locks before monsoon landfall in six weeks. She refuses. Then Brant's agents torch a warehouse looking for Pip. POV: Sable. Beat: reluctant alliance forms; love-against-duty theme ignites.

chapters.title: Crew of the Willing
chapters.summary: Sable puts it to a vote. Doss votes no, then packs his tools anyway. Marisol signs on for the names—the Erasure took her brothers. Pip claims the chest as inheritance. They cast off at night, running the first closed lock by moonlight while Brant watches from shore, letting them go—for now. POV: alternating Sable and Ivo. Beat: found family solidifies; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Locks Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo teaches Sable the old Vhalorian lock-signals carved into the stonework, and she realizes her late father was a keeper too—that this river ran in erased blood all along. The second lock's keeper, an old woman, recognizes Ivo's face and weeps, giving them passage and a warning: someone else went upstream two days ahead. POV: Sable. Beat: memory as inheritance; the personal stakes deepen.

chapters.title: Rapids Called the Judgment
chapters.summary: The Magpie runs the Judgment rapids with Ivo reading water-signs from the bow and Sable at the wheel in perfect, terrifying sync. They clear it—but lose their spare anchor chain and nearly lose Pip, who freezes at the rail. That night Ivo and Sable share watch, and something unspoken passes between them. POV: Sable. Beat: trust forged in white water; tenderness amid danger.

chapters.title: Brant's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brant catches them at a fueling depot—not with guns, but an offer: surrender the chest and he'll bury the crew's smuggling charges. Sable stalls. Privately, Doss urges taking the deal; Marisol threatens to mutiny if anyone does. The crew fractures. Meanwhile they learn the boat ahead belongs to Vessarin, a Vhalorian collaborator who sold out his own people. POV: Sable. Beat: duty vs. loyalty made literal; the middle-dark moment begins.

chapters.title: The Collaborator's Wake
chapters.summary: Vessarin's boat sabotages theirs at the third lock—cut mooring lines in the night, flooding the engine room. Doss takes scalding steam saving the boiler. Ivo reveals Vessarin betrayed his parents to the ministry forty years ago. Sable realizes Brant and Vessarin are working together, trading on the archive's location. POV: Ivo. Beat: rage and guilt; the enemy's shape becomes clear.

chapters.title: Monsoon Sky
chapters.summary: Weather reports confirm the monsoon makes landfall in nine days; after that, the upper gorge is suicide. Sable pushes the crew past exhaustion repairing the Magpie. Pip, feverish from a rope burn gone septic, confesses he's been copying the route-map—he wants to find his grandmother's village himself. POV: Pip. Beat: cost of the journey mounts; love expressed as stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Off the main channel, they find Pip's grandmother's village: officially never existed, yet foundations, an orchard gone wild, a schoolhouse bell still hanging. Marisol finds her brothers' names scratched into a doorframe. The crew understands what the archive means now—not politics, but people. POV: Marisol. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the emotional heart of the book.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Vessarin ambushes them in a narrow gorge, and Brant's gunboat seals the exit behind. In the firefight, Sable rams Vessarin's vessel into the rocks and takes a bullet graze across her ribs. Ivo pulls her from the water. They escape through a flood-tunnel only a Vhalorian pilot would know—Ivo navigating from childhood memory. POV: Ivo. Beat: love confessed in adrenaline; the net tightens.

chapters.title: What Sable Buried
chapters.summary: Feverish, Sable finally tells Ivo about her old crew—the Magpie's previous voyage, the capsizing she survived and four who didn't, the inquiry that blamed her. She captains alone because the river forgives nothing and neither does she. Ivo answers with why he never went home: some doors you're afraid to open. POV: Sable. Beat: mutual absolution begins; intimacy deepens beyond attraction.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: Above the last cataract, the canyon walls bear thousands of carved names—Vhalorians who walked here before the Erasure, a pilgrimage route to the source. Ivo finds his family name and cannot speak. They portage the boat overland using winches and sheer will, racing the rising brown water. POV: Ivo. Beat: awe and mourning; the destination feels holy.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Doss disappears with the astrolabe—revealed as Brant's informant since chapter four, coerced by threats against his daughter. Devastated, the crew presses on afoot through the final gorge as the monsoon's first outer bands hit. Sable refuses to hate him: 'He chose his kid. I'd have done the same.' POV: Doss. Beat: betrayal without villainy; duty's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the source cavern: a spring-fed vault where the archive waits—thousands of name-ledgers, the complete record of the erased. But Brant and Doss arrive by helicopter pad above, and Vessarin's surviving men hold the entrance. Standoff in the rain. Brant offers one last time: hand it over, everyone walks. POV: Sable. Beat: climax pressure; every debt comes due.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits full force; the gorge begins to flood. In the chaos, Vessarin tries to burn the archive rather than let history judge him, and Ivo takes a knife wound stopping him. Sable triggers the old flood-gates Vhalorians built to protect the vault, drowning the approach and sealing Brant's men out—with the crew inside, committed. POV: Ivo. Beat: sacrifice and irrevocability; the point of no return passed together.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Trapped inside by floodwater, the crew does the only thing left: they read. For hours, by lamplight, they read names aloud—Marisol's brothers, Pip's grandmother, Ivo's parents—while the river roars outside. Brant, listening through the flooded doorway, hears his own erased grandfather's name spoken and lowers his weapon. POV: Marisol. Beat: catharsis; memory defeats erasure not by force but by witness.

chapters.title: Inspector Brant's Report
chapters.summary: When waters recede, Brant faces his choice. He files a report declaring the source cavern collapsed and unrecoverable—officially closing the file forever—then quietly helps them carry out copies of the ledgers. Doss returns, expecting nothing; Sable gives him back the astrolabe for his daughter. POV: Brant. Beat: redemption through small mercies; duty redefined.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: The battered Magpie rides the swollen river home, carrying copied ledgers to be distributed among the scattered descendants. Ivo asks Sable what she'll do now that the delivery is done. She says the river gave her a crew again, and she doesn't intend to lose another one. First kiss at the wheel, rain on glass. POV: Sable. Beat: love chosen freely; the wound of solitude closes.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Current
chapters.summary: Months later, the Magpie runs a new route—unofficial ferry for people visiting places that don't exist on maps, guided by Ivo's archive knowledge and Pip's copied charts. A package arrives: fresh-cut orchard blossoms from the village, sent by hands unknown. Sable nails the old Vhalorian seal above her wheel and steers into the current. POV: Sable. Beat: resolution and renewal; the river remembers, and so do they.
